Senses.Explanation: 三界唯心 means the three realms are mind alone. 三界唯心 is the inherited formula that the three realms are mind alone. Zen records do not merely repeat it as doctrine: Mazu Daoyi links it to the dependence of perceived forms and mind; Huangbo Xiyun names it as a statement addressed to people holding wrong views rather than a final result; Luohan Guichen turns Fayan Wenyi's customary assertion into the concrete question whether a courtyard stone is inside or outside mind; Linji Yixuan invokes it and immediately points to the person presently hearing the teaching; Wuhuan Xingchong caps it with last night's rain wetting the moss; and Tianyin Yuanxiu comments that if the three realms are mind alone there can be no literal entering or leaving them.
Senses.Note: Preserve the formula but do not inflate 唯心 into an abstract metaphysical idealism. Several retained masters test, qualify, or redirect the inherited Buddhist wording instead of treating it as a self-sufficient Zen definition.
